title: per-request-claim-translation-and-region-bound-kms-proxy
author: Maya Lin
description:
Motivation: Customers asked for finer-grained tenant assertions on requests that can be translated into RBAC v2 decisions and enforced at the KMS proxy layer so keys cannot be used outside of pinned regions. This PR implements a per-request claim translation layer (CLAIM-T) that normalizes heterogeneous tenant claims from different identity providers, emits canonical assertion headers, and drives a lightweight region-bound KMS proxy that rejects key usage when the request's canonical region does not match the key's allowed residency.

What this change does: CLAIM-T: - Introduces a request interceptor that runs before auth decision and normalizes claim inputs (OIDC sub/azp, custom tenant attributes, service principal annotations) into a canonical assertion map (x-rd-assertion-*) used by RBAC v2 policy evaluation. - Adds linear mapping rules (config-driven) so teams can plug in provider-specific claim keys without code changes. Region-bound KMS proxy: - Adds a sidecar-like proxy component (kms-region-proxy) that validates that the requested CMK region matches the tenant assertion or an allowed fallback list. - Proxy emits immutable audit headers (x-rd-audit-kms-origin, x-rd-audit-region-assertion) for downstream auditors and the central audit-collector. - Integrates with existing CMK metadata service to cache key residency and fallback policies to keep latency <6ms p50 on the proxy path.

Compatibility and rollout: - Backwards compatible by default: when CLAIM-T mapping is empty, request flow remains unchanged. - Feature gated via a runtime flag (feature.claim_translation=true) and a per-tenant annotation to opt-in. - Canary rollout plan: enable for internal-sandbox tenants -> 5% production -> 25% -> 100%.

Testing and validation: - Unit tests for mapping rules and assertion normalization. - Integration tests exercising proxy rejection/allow flows including cross-region failover. - Load test on benchmark-lab to verify proxy adds <5% p95 latency at 1k rps.

Checklist: - [x] Mapping engine + config docs - [x] Assertion header schema (RFC-like doc in repo) - [x] KMS proxy implementation + cache - [x] End-to-end tests and canary rollout config - [x] Updated operator playbook for incident response when proxy rejects legitimate traffic

Notes: This PR intentionally keeps policy evaluation out of the proxy — the proxy only enforces region residency gates and emits canonical assertion headers. Full RBAC v2 decisions continue to happen in the policy-evaluator component; CLAIM-T makes policy inputs consistent across identity providers.

review_comments: Akhil Rao: Can the mapping rules be reloaded without a full service restart? This matters for on-call when identity provider mappings change.
Maya Lin (author): Mapping rules are watched from S3/config-store and applied atomically; added a test and doc note in configs/claim_translation_rules.yaml.
Elena Petrova: The proxy adds an extra network hop. Have we measured tail latency impact for small payloads?
Maya Lin (author): Yes — benchmark-lab runs showed +4% p95 on 1k rps with local cache warm; p99 impact stays <10ms. Added results to docs and a dashboard panel in observability-pack for the canary.
Jonas Becker: What happens for customers that use multi-region CMKs (replicated)? We should allow an explicit fallback list on key metadata.
Maya Lin (author): Implemented key metadata fallback list and preference order; added unit tests and a migration note for key metadata service.
